# Warden

Warden is an open-source sandbox runtime for MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers. It runs each local server in an OS sandbox so the process only sees the files, network hosts, and environment variables a policy explicitly grants. Everything else is denied. If no sandbox backend is available, Warden refuses to run the server unsandboxed.

Official name: Warden
Category: sandbox runtime for MCP servers
Site: https://warden.blog
Source: https://github.com/Prof-bilal/Warden
Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/warden-sandbox-cli
License: MIT
Price: $0
Creator: Abdullah Bilal (GitHub: Prof-bilal)
Who it is for: developers running local MCP servers they did not write

## What it does

- Sandboxes MCP servers on Linux (bubblewrap), macOS (Seatbelt), and Windows (AppContainer), with Docker as a fallback backend.
- Policies are deny-by-default YAML: filesystem read/write, network hosts, environment variable names, and resource limits.
- Commands include run, trace, init, logs, doctor, gateway, proxy, and Kubernetes manifest rendering.
- Audit logs record allowed and blocked file, network, and environment events.
- Warden is a local CLI. It does not provide a hosted HTTP API. MCP clients keep using stdio.
